extracted.intended_audience: King Philip II / Spanish royal administrators and colonial officials
extracted.subtask_description: A sixteenth-century relation and set of recommendations to the Spanish crown about navigation, military provisioning, governance, trade, and settlement policy for the Western Islands (the Philippines) and nearby regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voyage route and seasonal-wind planning
rubrics_metrics.description: "The best route is to sail strictly in the latitude in which lies the island that one wishes to reach; for in the season of the brisas, which is the right time to make the voyage, favorable stern winds are never wanting. The season for the brisas lasts from the end of October to the end of April. From the end of April to the end of October the vendaváls blow... he who wishes to return ought to take a higher degree of latitude."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan outbound voyages within the target island's latitude during the brisas (end Oct–end Apr). For return voyages use higher latitude to catch vendaváls (Apr–Oct). Use the seasonality of winds to ensure favorable stern winds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Port selection and shelter suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: "Nueva España has two ports in the South Sea. That which is called Acapulco is [very] good and can give shelter to many ships... It is in seventeen and one-half degrees of north latitude. The other is called Puerto de la Navidad; its entrance is shallow, and it can therefore give shelter to small ships only. It is in nineteen and one-third degrees of north latitude."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose Acapulco for large ships and heavy shelter; Puerto de la Navidad only for small vessels because of its shallow entrance. Take latitude into account when planning departure/arrival.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of repartimiento (reapportionment of Indians) to sustain colony
rubrics_metrics.description: "I have reapportioned and am reapportioning the Indians, as is done in Gautemala and other parts of the Indies... I beg your Majesty to favor this and send confirmation of it, because in no other way can this island be maintained for the present."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reapportioning indigenous labor (repartimientos) is presented as a necessary administrative measure to sustain the island and the military presence; requires royal confirmation to be effective and lawful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of soldier 'raids' as a means of support
rubrics_metrics.description: "These [raids] were wont to be made formerly, in order to support themselves; but they proved of great harm and prejudice to the natives; and by them God our Lord, and your Majesty were not served. With this remedy these evils cease."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forbid and remove reliance on raiding by soldiers for subsistence because it damages relations with natives and undermines royal service; replace with organized provisioning and repartimiento.

rubrics_metrics.name: Term limits for municipal officials (regidores)
rubrics_metrics.description: "I think it a matter very important to your Majesty's service that, for the present, there should be no perpetual regidores in these parts, but those who are elected annually; because in this way they will do their duties well... On the contrary, they will, if elected in perpetuity, become careless, as experience shows."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt annual election/renewal of regidores (town councilors) rather than perpetual appointments to avoid faction, maltreatment, and negligent administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection and reward of competent military officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations to favor individuals: e.g., Martin de Goiti 'worthy and deserving' of 'all favors' on account of 'qualit[ies] and his experience in warlike matters and the Christian spirit' and Juan de Salcedo deserving 'some favor' for services and sacrifices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant rewards, offices, or favors to those who have proven military competence, experience, fidelity, and Christian conduct; use merit and service record as criteria for appointments and rewards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governor appointment: must be respected and qualified
rubrics_metrics.description: "If this venture is to succeed... your Majesty must appoint a man to that office who will be respected and esteemed, and who possesses the necessary qualifications both for peace and war. I beg your Majesty not to make trial, especially in the case of those who are to participate in the administration of justice, of men from the Indias."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid experimental or locally untested appointments; choose a governor with authority, military and administrative competence, and standing so justice and safety can be secured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justice as the primary condition for safety
rubrics_metrics.description: "Every one asserts that the chief deficiency of that land is justice; and without justice there is no safety."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate colonial administration first by its administration of justice; remedying judicial deficiencies is central to achieving order and successful governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fort placement and defensive works criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Fort planned 'between the two arms of a river... the ground all the way to the fort is a swamp... enemies can approach the said fort only through the river, where are planted the above-mentioned gabions and artillery... The position is excellent, and such that it needs only a few men to defend it against many.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Site forts inland behind natural obstacles (swamps, river arms) to limit approaches, defend river entrances with gabions and artillery, and position to maximize defensive strength with minimal manpower; account for bar depth and navigable channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military staffing and provisioning for exploration and conquest
rubrics_metrics.description: "If your Majesty desires to have this land explored, I am at your service provided I be given two ships of about two hundred and fifty tons each, with forty soldiers to each vessel, and all the artillery, ammunition, and provisions that will be necessary... I will carry out all other orders that your Majesty may be pleased to give me."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify clear force and logistics requirements (ship tonnage, number of soldiers per vessel, artillery, ammo, provisions) before planning exploration or military expeditions; require ambassadorial authority where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for entering China and trade approach
rubrics_metrics.description: "To enter into this subject... more and better soldiers would be needful... The commerce with that land must be carried on with silver, which they value above all other things; and I am uncertain whether your Majesty will consent to this on account of having to send it to a foreign kingdom."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize China's reluctance toward strangers and the need for significant military force to engage; plan trade primarily in silver and weigh the political/economic costs of sending silver abroad.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spice trade strategic recommendation (Moluccas/cloves)
rubrics_metrics.description: "If your Majesty does not wish to continue the spice trade, on account of the great expense and the little profit that it now yields, or will yield in the future, I think that it would be advisable to withdraw the people from the islands... If your Majesty prefers the spices, I think that it would be better to break the agreement [with Portugal], since... three hundred and fifty thousand ducats would be gained in two ships going from Nueva España to those regions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess profitability of the spice trade; if marginal, consider withdrawal rather than continued expense; if pursued, consider breaking restrictive agreements to capture greater profits (economic cost–benefit framing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Slave acquisition and transfer proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: "It seems to me that it would be less troublesome, and that God would be better served, if the Spaniards bought these slaves and took them to Nueva España, where they would become Christians; they would thus supply the great need for slaves there."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposes buying local slaves for transfer to other colonies (Nueva España) to meet labor needs and ostensibly for Christianization—presented as administratively easier and beneficial to imperial needs (note: prescriptive colonial policy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of mineral wealth and labor economics
rubrics_metrics.description: "All the gold mines of this island are so poor that the natives offer their labor for a gold maes or three reals per month... It is therefore evident that it is not possible to save from the mines much gold... A slave can be bought for fifty reals."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate mines realistically: small yields and very low local labor costs mean mines may not be a profitable source of large returns; use local price examples when planning extraction or fiscal policy.
